what: Gap D follow-ups, all executed in CI 2026-08-22: (1) 6x-budget rerun on the 4 sub-bar seeds, (2) amplitude sweep s in {0.25..2} x 3 seeds, (3) first real-corpus lens run with selection-null control

budget_rerun.verdict: 3 of 4 sub-bar seeds flip to H1 at larger budget -> combined with the 15-seed sweep, 14/15 seeds clear the bar at sufficient budget. The sweep misses were optimizer starvation, not absence of effect.

amplitude_sweep.verdict: No amplitude threshold where H1 dies: the lens clears the bar at every s including 0.25. Delta_J grows with s for responsive seeds. Seed-10-style failures are HEADROOM, not seed identity: at s=0.25 seed 10 flips to +5.71 because identity_J drops to 1.09; whenever the identity chart already captures the signal (identity_J ~ 5), the lens cannot add 2 null-SDs.

real_corpus_lens.config: seed 20260822, n_null=20 curveball draws (20 trades/row), n_random=150, n_coord_rounds=20; PC3-as-field per the documented spectral-defocus convention; anti-caustic guard on real AND all null designs

identity.note: at the identity chart the real corpus L=3 share sits BELOW its fixed-margin null

selection_null_control.design: For each of 10 curveball draws, treat that draw as the optimization target (--control-index i) and optimize the lens under identical selection pressure; the real corpus becomes a null member.
selection_null_control.verdict: Real delta_J (+126.1) is ~4.9x the strongest control and ~25x the control median. Margin-noise under identical selection pressure cannot fake the result: controls can reach high shares (max 0.54) but cannot simultaneously collapse the rest of the ensemble to a tight low-share cluster. The lens finds genuinely corpus-specific L=3 structure beyond fixed margins.
